title: Hub 重启：Agent 自动重连、Session/Desired State 重建与权威源收敛

cases.title: SYS-03 Hub 重启：Agent 自动重连、Session 重建、Desired State 不丢
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

covered_dimensions.layer: hub unit restart / hub sqlite / gateway sessions / 4 protected repair Agents
description: `systemctl stop/start nodesteer-hub-repair-20260930-101945.service` on 192.168.100.209: caller-visible /healthz and /readyz stopped answering (outage observed from the operator workstation), MainPID changed, and the binary sha256 stayed 164ea4ac...

All 4 protected repair Agents went through orphan-online reset at Hub start and reconnected by themselves to online/synced with global_revision >= the revision of a Desired State change committed just before the restart (timeline sampled every 1s).

Hub persistence survived: revision_sequence stayed >= the pre-restart revision, the owned script/task rows and their revision_changes rows were still present after the restart, PRAGMA quick_check = ok, and the owned child Agent reconciled exactly the one logical change with no duplicate Execution.

remaining_or_limitations: The 4 protected repair Agents had already applied the pre-restart Desired State change before the unit was stopped (they were connected when it was written), so their evidence covers session rebuild, retained applied revision and automatic reconnection; the "lag while disconnected, then reconcile on reconnect" direction is proven by the harness-owned child Agent, which was cut from the Hub before the change.
The observed Hub unavailability was short (~1.3 s: HTTP unanswered and TCP refused). A long outage beyond the Hub heartbeat timeout was not exercised in this batch.

The repair Hub was restarted once in the reported run (twice across both attempts); management API sessions live in Hub memory and therefore do not survive the restart - the next call returned 401 and was re-authenticated once by the harness client.

cases.title: SYS-17 Agent 重连前不宣告 READY，完成 Reconciliation 后再 READY
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

covered_dimensions.layer: owned child Agent ready gate / harness frame proxy / hub execution dispatch
description: Reconnect order on the wire: HELLO -> HELLO_ACK -> SYNC_REQUEST -> SYNC_RESPONSE -> SYNC_ACK; the harness held the Hub->Agent SYNC_RESPONSE(s) so the Reconciliation window stayed open.
While the reply was withheld the owned child was online on the Hub but its applied revision was still the pre-restart one and its local store still held the old script sha: no READY.

A real manual Run dispatched in that window produced a real BLOCKED Execution whose block_reason is the Agent's own "agent not ready (reconciling)" gate - the business-level proof that READY was not claimed.
After the reply was released the Agent applied the sync (SYNC_ACK applied_rev = Hub revision), its reported revision caught up, and the next manual Run returned SUCCESS with the nonce marker.

remaining_or_limitations: READY is an internal Agent state; it was observed through its product-level effects (rejected dispatch in the Reconciliation window, accepted dispatch after it) and the Hub-visible applied revision, not by reading Agent memory.
The Reconciliation window was widened by holding SYNC_RESPONSE frames on the harness's own frame proxy for its own child Agent; no product code and no protected Agent was changed.

cases.title: INV-01 Hub 是 Desired State 唯一权威源
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

covered_dimensions.layer: hub script authority / owned child store / hub restart persistence
description: The operator changed the script on the Hub while the owned child was cut from the Hub; the child kept its stale copy and its old local revision, i.e. the Agent never became the source of the value.
After the restart the Hub still served exactly the operator-written object (same sha256/revision) and the Agent converged to it on reconnection - Hub -> Agent only.
Hub rows and revision_changes were unchanged by the Agent side across the restart; no Agent-originated Desired State write path was observed in the frame ledger.

remaining_or_limitations: Authority was exercised through the script (Desired State) object path; the Execution/Journal upload path is a separate direction of the protocol and was out of scope for this invariant.

cases.title: AR-01 Hub Restart；恢复后幂等、持久化、Desired State 与实际状态一致
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

covered_dimensions.layer: hub restart / real executions on a protected repair node / idempotency
description: Real execution before the restart on protected native-2: terminal SUCCESS, stdout carried the nonce pre marker, exactly one Hub row.
Real execution after the restart on the same protected node: terminal SUCCESS, stdout carried the nonce post marker, exactly one Hub row - the restart did not lose or duplicate work.

After a settle window the Task had exactly 2 Executions on the target node and 2 on the owned child (one BLOCKED during Reconciliation, one SUCCESS after it): no duplicated Execution and no half state.
Desired State and actual state agreed after the restart: the Hub script sha256/revision were the operator-written values and both the protected node and the owned child had applied them.

remaining_or_limitations: Hub restart was performed once, on the single authorised repair unit; the primary :8080 Hub and every Agent service kept their original MainPIDs (recorded read-only before and after).

harness_seams.authority: management writes only to repair http://192.168.100.209:18080
harness_seams.hub_restart: only nodesteer-hub-repair-20260930-101945.service was stopped/started once; nodesteer-hub.service (:8080) and all Agent units untouched
harness_seams.owned_child: one harness-owned child Agent on native-1 (exact repair Agent binary d55dc5cd...) behind a harness-owned frame proxy on 192.168.100.170
harness_seams.ready_gate: SYNC_RESPONSE frames were held on the harness frame proxy so the Reconciliation window could be observed and exercised by a real manual Run

post_run_additions: evidence/phase0-untouched-units-after.json - identical read-only unit probe repeated AFTER the batch; compared with evidence/phase0-untouched-units.json it shows every protected Agent and the primary Hub kept the same MainPID, while only the repair Hub MainPID changed (authorised restart).

evidence/attempt01-harness-bug/ - artifacts of the first attempt, kept unmodified. It failed on a harness bug (the repair-Hub restart invalidated the management API session, so the client did not re-authenticate; plus a %-formatting bug in the child remove helper). Both were fixed and the batch was re-run completely (EXIT=0); the report above is the second, complete run.

Repair-Hub restart count for the whole sys-b01 batch: 2 (one per attempt). Attempt 1 restarted the unit once (MainPID 5952 -> 97295) and then aborted on the harness bug; attempt 2 restarted it again (MainPID 97295 -> 97389) and completed. The unit is active at the end of the batch and /healthz, /readyz both answer 200; no protected Agent unit and no primary-Hub unit was ever restarted.

Product observation (not a failure): the repair Hub keeps management sessions in memory, so the first API call after the restart returned 401 "invalid or expired session" and the client re-authenticated once. Recorded in evidence/phase6-post-restart.json -> management_session_after_restart.
